lawyer:
Abdus Salam Khan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Petitioners (In all the cases). 
Abdul Quayum, Senior Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Respondents (In all the cases)
parties:
Ramesh Chandra Barman and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Iswar Kalachan Jieu Thakur and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment: 3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement contending that four sons of Janaki, who on obtaining citizenship had been living in India permanently, having refused to conduct sheba puja of the deity, Kali Pada Dutta, after the death of Mallika Sandari Dutta conducted the sheba puja and requested his remaining four brothers to constitute a committee comprising of six members and the above four brothers having refused the said request, Kali Pada Dutta filed the above Title Suit No 39 of 1959 seeking declaration that his above four brothers, who were made defendants in the above suit, ceased to be the shebait of the deity and also praying for removal of the above four brothers from the shebaitship of the said deity and also prayed for a scheme for the management of the properties of the deity and for worship of the deity in conformity with the terms and conditions of the deed of endowment and the then learned Munsif after hearing, decreed the above suit in terms of the solenama dated 17-7-1965 by which Kali Pada Dutta became shebait and Md Nasiruddin became the manager of the deity; then Sremanta Kumar Dutta, an Indian citizen and one of the sons of Kali Kishore Dutta, who died in India on 29-9-65, came to Bangladesh and filed Title Appeal No 305 of 1965 against the above compromise decree and the above appeal: being dismissed after hearing, he moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No 9 of 1994; after the death of Sreemanta Kumar Dutta his son Biswajit Dutta alias Bhulu, the plaintiff  No. 2, came to Bangladesh from India in the year 1972 and was living in Bangladesh illegally; Binode Behari Dutta went to India for study with Bangladeshi passport and student visa and when his father Kali Pada Dutta fell ill he came back to Bangladesh to look after his father and then took his father to India and then Kali Pada having died in India on 31-12-97, Binode Behari Dutta became the shebait in place of Kali Pada Dutta and then he by power of attorney dated 9-7-98 appointed Ramesh Chandra Barman, the defendant, to look after the property of the deity and so the plaintiff No. 2 has no right to file this suit. The learned Joint District Judge, after hearing, by judgment and decree dated 8-1-2005 decree the suit in part i.e. only declaring that the power of attorney executed by Binode Behari Dutta on 9-7-98 in favour of Ramesh Chandra Barman, the defendant, is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs and rejected the prayer of permanent injunction. As against that the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 104 of 2005 on the ground that the suit should have been decreed in full by passing the decree of permanent injunction as well and the defendant preferred Title Appeal No.108 of 2005 on the ground that the suit ought to have been dismissed. The learned Additional District Judge, who heard both the appeals analogously, by judgment and decree dated 13-9-2005 allowed Title Appeal No. 104 of 2005 decreeing the suit in full i.e. granting decree of permanent injunction as well and dismissed Title Appeal No. 108 of 2005. Then both the parties moved the High Court Division and obtained Rules in Civil Revision Nos. 4243 and 4244 of 2005.
